subject: Close timeline: MAP alignment, slippage scenarios & escalation request
messages:
From: Ellena Park <ellena.park@helixhealth.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Helix Health Procurement <procurement@helixhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Close timeline: MAP alignment & slippage scenarios

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the MAP you shared last week. We reviewed internally and a few risk items are starting to push our internal acceptance checkpoints. At a high level: procurement sign-off looks OK, but our integration testing slot is now tight due to a dependent vendor delay (Tom Gibbs' team).

We need a short list of slippage scenarios from your side that map to (a) acceptance impact, (b) procurement conditions (credit/penalty requests), and (c) fallback options. Can you also include a proposed contingency for preserving the target close date of 2027-06-30?

Prefer a 30-minute call this week — I can do Tue/Wed after 1pm PT.

Ellena

Helix Health

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Ellena Park <ellena.park@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Close timeline: MAP alignment & slippage scenarios

Hi Ellena — thanks for the note and the heads-up. I pulled together three concise scenarios and attached a short scenario matrix (slippage-scenarios.pdf) plus an updated MAP (MAP_v2.xlsx). Key points up-front:

- Scenario A — 'On Track': no change to acceptance windows, assumes Tom's vendor completes integration by 6/10. Impact: close remains 6/30. Contingency: reserved surge slot for final acceptance.
- Scenario B — 'Soft Slip' (2-week): integration delayed -> acceptance window slides 2 weeks. Impact: close target moves to 7/14 unless procurement approves parallel sign-off with partial go-live. Contingency: prefix caching and staged feature cutover.
- Scenario C — 'Material Slip' (6-week): vendor delay persists -> acceptance window slides 6 weeks. Impact: close to ~8/15; requires procurement flexibility on payment milestones and option for service credit.

Immediate asks from our side:
1) Confirm whether Helix Procurement is open to a partial acceptance + staggered billing approach for Scenario B.
2) If Scenario C becomes likely, would Helix consider a 60/40 milestone split to keep momentum?

I'm proposing a 30-minute call Wed 1:30–2:00 PM PT to walk through the matrix. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and a short runbook for the call.

Attachments: MAP_v2.xlsx (MAP refresh), slippage-scenarios.pdf (3-up scenario matrix)

Best,
Mateo Alvarez | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwood.com | +1 650-555-2291

Looping in a quick escalation note. Mateo — thanks for the scenarios. From a commercial stance we should prepare an escalation-decision-log (attached stub) and a limited exec escalation offer. My recommendation:

- Prepare an exec escalation packet that includes the scenario matrix, a proposed service-credit framework if Helix needs a hard commitment on an earlier close, and a clear acceptance fallback (staged go-live).
- Ask Ops to identify one surge slot (2 days) the week of 7/10 that we could use as a final acceptance window if needed.

If Helix confirms Scenario B as likely we should be ready to offer conditional credits (up to 10%) tied to specific missed milestones instead of full-scale repricing. I'll own the credit mechanics and decision log.

Attachment: escalation-decision-log.txt

-Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ellena Park <ellena.park@helixhealth.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Close timeline: MAP alignment & slippage scenarios — Exec escalation

Ellena / Team — thanks for the candid context. I'm escalating to confirm an executive remediation path and to make a firm offer to keep the deal moving without re-pricing. Key commitments from Redwood:

- Conditional Service Credit: up to 10% applied to first invoice if we miss the agreed final acceptance milestone and impacted features are not delivered per the agreed staggered acceptance plan.
- Staged Acceptance Plan: we will provide a narrow acceptance checklist for partial sign-off so Helix can start limited production earlier for lower-risk features.
- Surge Acceptance Window: Ops committed to identifying a surge slot w/in the 7/10 week; if that slot is used, Redwood will prioritize support resources on-site remotely.

Next steps: Mateo, Ben — please finalize the exec-escalation-note (attached) and the scenario matrix bullet points. Ellena — if Helix can confirm preference for Scenario B vs. C by EOD Friday (6/04), we will finalize the escalation packet and prepare a DocuSign addendum to the MAP for procurement.

Attachments: exec-escalation-note.pdf

Thanks,
Marissa Cole | Head of Customer Success (region West)
